To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
IL-17 produced by γδT cells promotes tumor growth via suppression of antitumoral immunity and induction of myeloid derived suppressor cells.
IL-17 produced by γδT cells promotes tumor growth via suppression of CD8+ T cell responses and enhancement of MDSC infiltration.
IL-17-producing γδ T cell is critical for tumor progression in a mouse model of HCC, and that IL-17 promotes tumor growth by inducing MDSC infiltration and enhancing their suppressive activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of action of the proinflammatory cytokine interleukin (IL-17A) in tumor immunity.
the role of interleukin (IL-17A) produced by γδT cells in tumor development.
the mechanism of how IL-17 produced by γδT cells promotes hepatocellular carcinoma, and the mechanism of how γδT cells, MDSC, and tumor cells interact through IL-17 production.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
IL-17 produced by γδT cells promotes tumor growth through suppression of anticumour responses, especially CD 8 T-cell responses.
IL-17 produced by γδT cells promotes tumor growth through suppression of antiviral immunity and induction of MDSC.

IL-17 promotes tumor growth through the following mechanisms: 1) IL-17 induces CXCL5 production from tumor cells, 2) CXCL5 attracts MDSC to the tumor site in a CXCR2-dependent manner, 3) MDSC suppresses antitumor immunity, 4) MDSC induces IL-17-producing γδ T cell through the production of IL-23 and IL-1β, and 5) IL-17 enhances production of IL-17,
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
IL-17 produced by γδ-T cells is a critical factor for the development and progression of HCC.
IL-17-producing γδ T cell promotes tumor growth by enhancing the infiltration and suppressive function of myeloid derived suppressor cells in a positive-feedback fashion.
IL-17-producing γδ T cell, myeloid-derived supressor cell (MDSC) and tumor cells form a positive feedback loop to promote hepatocellular carcinoma growth through IL-17 production.
The main takeaway from our work is that

IL-17 produced by γδT cells is a tumor-promoting cytokine, and that the mechanism is through suppression of antiviral T cell responses, especially CD4 T cells, by inducing the accumulation of MDSCs in the tumor micro-environment.
IL-17 plays a key role in tumor immunity.
IL-17 is a key factor in promoting tumor growth.
